title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and templates for hiring, new-employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and essential manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and frontline managers. Follow the checklists and templates below to ensure a consistent, fair, and high-quality experience for candidates and employees.

Table of contents:
1) Hiring process and scorecards
2) Interviewer responsibilities and best practices
3) Offer and close checklist
4) New hire onboarding: 0-90 plan
5) Performance and feedback cycles
6) Manager guide: 1:1s, calibration, career growth
7) Key policies and templates

1) Hiring process and scorecards
Introduction:
- Goal: hire with speed, fairness, and high quality while minimizing bias and ensuring consistent evaluation across teams.
- Ownership: Hiring manager + people-ops partner.

Stages (recommended):
1. Requisition raised (Hiring manager) -- template in the Recruiting portal.
2. Phone screen (recruiter) -- culture fit, role fit, salary expectations.
3. Technical/functional interviews (2-3 interviews) -- role-specific scorecards.
4. Hiring manager interview -- team fit and role-readiness.
5. Final onsite / loop (can be virtual) -- cross-functional stakeholders and hiring manager.
6. Decision and offer.

Scorecard fields (use for every interviewer):
- Role: technical / product / manager / IC.
- Core competencies (3-5): e.g., system design, coding, model evaluation, communication.
- Rating scale: 1 (insufficient) -- 5 (exceptional).
- Must-hire flags: 'yes' if candidate meets non-negotiable criteria.
- Notes: evidence for ratings and any concerns.

Diversity & inclusive hiring requirements:
- Every req must have at least one diverse-sourced candidate in the final 3 candidates.
- Interview panels should include diverse perspectives where possible.
- People-ops will run slate reviews for senior roles (director+).

2) Interviewer responsibilities and best practices
Before the interview:
- Read the candidate's resume and scorecard.
- Prepare 3-5 focused questions tied to the role competencies.
- Agree on scope with the hiring manager (what to evaluate).

During the interview:
- Start with 2 minutes of introductions and set expectations.
- Ask behavioral and technical questions; probe for examples and trade-offs.
- Take structured notes on the scorecard; capture evidence for ratings.
- Avoid off-limits questions (personal, health, family status, citizenship).

After the interview:
- Complete the scorecard within 24 hours.
- Provide concrete evidence for scores (code samples, design trade-offs, metrics).

Calibration and debriefs:
- Hiring manager organizes a debrief within 48 hours of final loop.
- Use scorecards to drive decision; people-ops will spot-check for fairness and consistent bar application.

3) Offer and close checklist
Offer components to confirm before sending:
- Approved compensation band and level (people-ops compensation partner).
- Total cash, equity grant philosophy and expected grant (range), sign-on bonus (if applicable).
- Target start date and relocation budget (if applicable).
- Manager points of contact for pre-boarding.

Offer process:
1. Hiring manager drafts offer rationale and shares with people-ops.
2. People-ops issues official offer letter via ATS.
3. Recruiter schedules a call to review offer and answer questions.
4. Negotiation handled by hiring manager with people-ops support.
5. Candidate accepts -- initiate background checks and pre-boarding tasks.

Decline & feedback policy:
- If declining, send a timely, respectful rejection. Recruiters provide feedback coaching to managers if requested.

4) New hire onboarding: 0-90 plan
Purpose: accelerate time-to-impact through structured orientation, role clarity, and relationships.

Pre-day 1 (recruiter + IT + manager):
- Confirm start date, equipment order, and access (Slack, GitHub, Jira, internal docs).
- Send welcome packet: company handbook, team org chart, 30/60/90 template.
- Create 30/60/90 goals draft with manager.

Day 1:
- Welcome meeting with manager (30-60m): role overview, immediate priorities, first-week goals.
- HR orientation: benefits, payroll, code of conduct, security briefing.
- IT provisioning check: laptop, VPN, KMS access request submitted.
- Team welcome: quick standup intro and assigned buddy.

Week 1:
- Complete mandatory trainings: security, data handling, privacy.
- Meet top 5 stakeholders (15-30m each).
- Deliverable: first-week readout and 30/60/90 draft.

30/60/90 template (manager to co-author):
- 30-day: learning goals, access completed, small contribution (bug fix / doc / test).
- 60-day: ownership of a small project, cross-team communication established.
- 90-day: measurable impact (feature delivered / performance improvement / operationalization).

Manager responsibilities during onboarding:
- Weekly 1:1s for first 12 weeks.
- Weekly quick sync with buddy.
- Provide incremental feedback and public recognition for early wins.

Onboarding KPIs (people-ops monitors):
- Time to first PR/commit (target: 14 days).
- Time to first independent feature (target: 60 days).
- New hire experience score (NPS survey at day 14 and day 90; target >= 70).

5) Performance and feedback cycles
Cycle cadence:
- Continuous feedback: ongoing 1:1s and ad hoc feedback.
- Quarterly check-ins (informal written summary).
- Formal mid-year review and end-of-year performance review (calibration + leveling).

Performance rubric elements:
- Role competence: technical/functional skills and output quality.
- Ownership & execution: delivery consistency and prioritization.
- Collaboration & communication: cross-team effectiveness.
- Growth & leadership: mentoring, initiative, and skill development.

Review process (timeline):
1. Self-assessment submitted 2 weeks prior to review meeting.
2. Manager assessment & evidence compilation.
3. Calibration meeting within org to align ratings and calibration notes.
4. Feedback delivery meeting with employee (manager).
5. Goal-setting for next cycle; update career plan.

Rating scale and calibration guidance:
- Use a 5-point scale mapped to expectations: 1 (does not meet) to 5 (consistently exceeds).
- Ratings must be evidence-backed (examples, metrics, impact).
- Calibration seeks to remove manager bias and ensure consistent leveling across teams.

Performance improvement & support:
- For gaps, managers should document concerns in a private coaching plan early (30-60 days).
- If improvement not observed, escalate to a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR/people-ops involvement (documented goals, support, timeline).

6) Manager guide: 1:1s, calibration, career growth
1:1 best practices:
- Cadence: weekly 30-60 minutes.
- Structure: check-in (personal), status, blockers, feedback, career/capstone topic.
- Record actions and decisions in the shared 1:1 doc; follow up on commitments within a week.

Career conversations and leveling:
- Have dedicated career conversations at least twice a year.
- Use the People Ops career framework (link in related_pages) to map expectations for ICs and managers.
- When recommending level changes, provide evidence (impact, scope, mentorship) and notify people-ops at least 30 days prior to performance cycle close.

Calibration & promotion process:
- Managers submit promotion packets with a narrative, evidence, and peer feedback.
- Promotions reviewed by a cross-functional promotions committee (people-ops, peer managers, and senior leader).
- Promotions should include a clear transition plan for ramp and communication.

Handling sensitive situations:
- Terminations, allegations of misconduct, or legal-sensitive matters must be escalated to people-ops and legal immediately.
- Follow the incident and incurrence playbooks in the security-and-compliance space for evidence preservation and confidentiality.

7) Key policies and templates
Remote & hybrid work:
- Redwood is remote-first with team-level hybrid options. Managers define in-office expectations aligned to role needs and document them in the team handbook.

Time off and leaves:
- PTO: competitive accrual; managers approve operational coverage.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (policy in benefits docs).
- Extended leave: case-by-case with people-ops liaison.

Code of conduct & workplace behavior:
- All employees must adhere to Redwood's Code of Conduct and anti-harassment policy.

Security & data handling basics for new hires (required trainings):
1. InfoSec Basics & Phishing (30m).
2. Data Classification & Handling (45m).
3. Model & Customer Data Safeguards (30m).

Templates (appendix):
- Sample scorecard questions (technical, product, manager).
- Offer rationale template (role, comp band, business justification).
- 30/60/90 goal template (editable doc link).
- 1:1 meeting note template (shared doc link).

Appendix: sample interviewer script (30-minute technical screen)
1. 2m -- quick intros and context.
2. 3m -- candidate background & high-level fit.
3. 20m -- live problem / case study (candidate talks through design / code / evaluation).
4. 3m -- clarifying questions & close.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ):
Q: Who owns the final hiring decision?
A: The hiring manager owns the decision; people-ops partners ensure compliance with process and compensation guardrails.

Q: What if the candidate requests a remote accommodation or visa sponsorship?
A: Flag to people-ops early; sponsorship cases require legal and people-ops review before offers.

Governance and review cadence for this playbook:
- People-ops will review and update this playbook annually or on major policy changes.

Contact and escalation:
- For hiring process questions: people-ops hiring team (hire@redwood-inference.internal).
- For compensation: comp-team@redwood-inference.internal.
- For urgent employee relations: hr-escalations@redwood-inference.internal.

End of document.
